mechanism_narrative: Sequential declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicate ongoing suppression of routine commuting and errands; each additional week with transit below -75 and workplaces below -70 reduces retail footfall, producing lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -70.3 to -80.0 and WORKPLACES fell from -62.6 to -71.9 over the four weeks ending t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next 28-day mean is higher than last 28-day mean while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain at or below t-0w levels.

mechanism_narrative: Once RESIDENTIAL exceeds 29 percent above baseline, at-home saturation is reached; households begin non-essential retail trips despite restrictions, causing RETAIL_REC to rise from its trough over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 24.9 to 29.0 over the four weeks ending t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next 14-day mean is lower than last 14-day mean even when RESIDENTIAL stays at or above 29.0.

mechanism_narrative: The joint condition of TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both falling by less than 2 points week-on-week signals the peak of lockdown stringency; retail mobility then recovers as policy easing follows over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES weekly declines each <= 2 points
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT weekly change slowed from -6.6 to -1.0 and WORKPLACES from -8.0 to 0.0 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next 28-day mean is lower than last 28-day mean despite TRANSIT and WORKPLACES weekly declines each being <= 2 points.

mechanism_narrative: Under tightening restrictions, GROCERY_PHARM is the primary permitted retail channel; its deepening decline indicates reduced shopping frequency, which spills over into lower RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from -35.9 to -49.9 over the four weeks ending t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next 28-day mean is higher than last 28-day mean while GROCERY_PHARM remains at or below -47.0.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction of PARKS and RESIDENTIAL captures risk perception: when PARKS rises while RESIDENTIAL stabilizes, households shift from home to outdoor activity and then to retail, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly change >= +3 points and RESIDENTIAL weekly change <= +0.5 points
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS changed from -66.9 to -67.7 and RESIDENTIAL from 28.0 to 29.0 in the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next 7-day mean is lower than last 7-day mean when PARKS weekly change is >= +3 points and RESIDENTIAL weekly change is <= +0.5 points.

mechanism_narrative: Spring weather normally lifts PARKS mobility, but lockdown restrictions keep parks deeply below baseline; the absence of a park rebound signals that outdoor substitution is not drawing consumers back to retail, so RETAIL_REC stays low over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS remained between -60.3 and -67.7 over the four weeks ending t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next 14-day mean is higher than last 14-day mean while PARKS remains at or below -60.0.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM is a leading indicator of essential-trip normalization; as grocery and pharmacy mobility stabilizes with weekly changes under 2 points, retail mobility follows with a recovery over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly change <= 2 points in absolute value
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM weekly changes were -11.7, +0.3, and -2.6 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next 28-day mean is lower than last 28-day mean while GROCERY_PHARM weekly change is <= 2 points in absolute value.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES falls below -70, workplace closures force consumers to consolidate trips and eliminate commute-linked shopping, reducing RETAIL_REC over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES reached -71.9 in t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC next 7-day mean is higher than last 7-day mean while WORKPLACES remains at or below -70.0.
